drug_class: PARP inhibitor (a type of targeted cancer therapy)
purpose: Talazoparib is used to treat certain types of breast cancer in adults who have a specific inherited gene mutation called BRCA. It is used when the cancer has spread to other parts of the body or cannot be removed with surgery. Your doctor will test for this gene mutation before starting treatment.
how_it_works: Your cancer cells have a broken repair system because of the BRCA gene mutation, which means they already struggle to fix their own DNA damage. Talazoparib works by blocking a protein called PARP, which cancer cells rely on to survive. By blocking this protein, the medication causes cancer cells to break down and die, while having less effect on normal healthy cells.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include feeling very tired or weak, nausea, hair thinning or loss, low blood cell counts (which can cause anemia, increased risk of infection, or easy bruising or bleeding), headache, decreased appetite, vomiting, and diarrhea. Low blood counts are very common, so your doctor will check your blood regularly.
warnings: Talazoparib can cause seriously low blood counts, which may require a blood transfusion or dose adjustment — tell your doctor right away if you feel extremely tired, look pale, or notice unusual bleeding or bruising. It can harm an unborn baby, so women must use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 7 months after the last dose. Men with female partners who could become pregnant should also use contraception. Do not breastfeed while taking this medication. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, as some drugs can interact with talazoparib.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one 1 mg capsule taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. Swallow the capsule whole — do not open, crush, or chew it. Try to take it at the same time each day. If you miss a dose, skip it and take your next dose as scheduled — never take two doses at once to make up for a missed one.
